newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH LIBERAL FARM MINISTER DISMISSED.
newsitem.headline: POLISH LIBERAL FARM MINISTER DISMISSED.

text.p: Poland's president sacked the liberal Farm Minister and Deputy Premier Roman Jagielinski on Thursday after majority of his Peasant Party lost confidence in him following a power struggle inside the group.
"The president, asked by the prime minister, recalled on April 10 Mr. Roman Jagielinski from the posts of agriculture minister and deputy prime minister," the president's press office statement said.

The post is likely to remain vacant for some time because Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz is dissatisfied with the Peasants' candidate for the post, a little-known politician Jaroslaw Kalinowski, a source close to the government said.
"Until the coalition parties sort things out..., one of the current deputy ministers would be the acting minister," the source, who asked not to be named, said.

Cimoszewicz was forced to ask for the dismissal of Jagielinski, the leader of the more market-oriented faction in the co-ruling Polish Peasant Party (PSL), after the minister lost the support of the majority of the group's leadership.
The majority -- led by Peasants' president Waldemar Pawlak, representing small farm owners keen to uphold state protection of agriculture -- have attacked Jagielinski's farm policies.
They accused him of policies resulting in a food trade deficit last year and low grain prices for domestic farmers, allegations which many economic analysts said were unfounded.
European Union diplomats have praised Jagielinski for his plans to modernise the countryside and cut the number of farms to below one million from the current more than two million.
Poland's obsolete agriculture is seen as a major obstacle to the country's accession to the EU.
Cimoszewicz -- member of the ruling coalition's more pro-market party, the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance -- defended Jagielinski and delayed his dismissal for many weeks.
He finally bowed to the pressure when the Peasants began to bloc work of the coalition by failing to attend meetings.
But Cimoszewicz's refusal to name Jaroslaw Kalinowski the new farm minister might stir another conflict in the coalition, which survived nearly four years despite frequent raws.

Analysts say the coalition should hold until parliamentary elections due around September, in which rightist and centrist parties rooted in the Solidarity movement will challenge the ex-communists and Peasants.
